title: A Confession for the Inheritance Revisited
premise: Estate lawyer Elodie Villalobos is hired to probate the will of reclusive heiress Marguerite Ashcombe, only to discover a second, contradictory will dated after the first — and a confession letter postmarked the day after the funeral naming Elodie herself as its intended recipient. As she traces the letter's author through the dead woman's household, she realizes the killer is someone with access to her own case files, feeding her just enough truth to keep her complicit. The trap Elodie sets — a falsified codicil announcing a hidden heir — flushes out the killer: Marguerite's devoted caretaker, who murdered her to protect a secret adoption that would have disinherited him. In the end, Elodie must choose between handing over evidence that could free a wrongfully imprisoned man and preserving her license, and she chooses justice outside the law.
about_author: Orsen Dunmore is the pen name of a former probate clerk who spent eleven years watching families tear themselves apart over paper. Dunmore writes mysteries from a farmhouse in Vermont, where the wills are simpler but the grudges run just as deep.

chapters.title: The Second Signature
chapters.summary: Elodie Villalobos opens the Ashcombe estate and finds two wills — one notarized, one handwritten, both authentic-looking, each cutting out the other's beneficiaries. That night, an unsigned confession arrives, postmarked the day after Marguerite's funeral, addressed to Elodie by name though no one knew she'd taken the case. Told from Elodie's POV; the emotional beat is professional confidence curdling into unease as she realizes the letter writer knows her habits intimately.

chapters.title: What the House Remembers
chapters.summary: Elodie interviews the household — the bitter nephew, the evasive solicitor, the gentle caretaker Tomas Reyes — while cross-checking dates against the confession's cryptic references to 'the nursery' and 'the winter of the fire.' A parallel thread reveals a man convicted of Marguerite's sister's death decades ago, still insisting he's innocent. Elodie's POV; the beat shifts from investigation to dread as she recognizes details in the letter that were never public — details that exist only in her case files.

chapters.title: A Codicil for Ghosts
chapters.summary: Certain the killer is watching her work, Elodie drafts a fake codicil revealing a hidden heir and lets it 'leak' through her insecure assistant. The bait works too well: within hours her office is ransacked, and the caretaker Tomas appears at her door holding the confession's missing second page — confessing to protect the adopted son Marguerite secretly raised, whose inheritance the old will would have erased. Elodie's POV; the beat is the vertigo of realizing her cleverness has made her an accessory.

chapters.title: Probate of the Heart
chapters.summary: Tomas gives Elodie proof that the imprisoned man was innocent and that Marguerite, dying, had begged him to bury the truth rather than shame the family. When police close in on Tomas, Elodie surrenders the exculpatory evidence anonymously, freeing the wrongfully convicted man while letting the law take Tomas on its own terms. Final chapter alternates Elodie's POV with excerpts of the confession itself; the closing beat is quiet reckoning — justice served, but never cleanly, and Elodie signing off the estate knowing some inheritances are debts.
